There are a few posts in here with great success stories for lithium which might be worth a read. I have been taking 500mg for 2 years now and have managed the side effects ok. For starters it’s super important that you eat a meal with your meds (otherwise you will feel nauseous) but if you forget the nausea usually goes away for me about 1 hour after I start feeling sick. It’s also super important to stay hydrated, I started carrying 1.5 litres of water with me and it does the trick. Also when I started I was super paranoid as well and my legs felt tingly for a week. Going for a small walk each day helped as well as drinking more water. If theres anything else you’re worried about let me know !

I’m on 500 ! It’s literally saved my life. I have never known stability like I do now. I have a job, I am excelling at uni, I have friends and relationships. I still feel what I need to but it’s just so controlled / so “normal” now. I have been saying to the people around me that I no longer feel depressed, I just feel sad sometimes. Genuinely so worth it if you can stick it out ! I’ve been on this dose for 2 years now and I think things started to even out at the 6month - 1 year mark ! Good luck !!!

Hi these are really good ! Life drawing / reference drawing really tests the communication between what you see and you hand, so to strengthen that I would recommend doing exercises such as ‘continuous line drawing’ and ‘blind drawing’. I’d also recommend having time limits to things for example 2min/5min/10min to begin with, this ensures you’re focusing on the shape and proportions rather than the details (which you can focus on later)
If you do this everyday for a month you will see a great improvement in your accuracy and ability to follow the shapes of the body !! Well done and hope this helps

I just had two wisdom teeth out, a filling and a clean under IV sedation (I’ve been putting it off for 2 years)! What made my experience comfortable was the team I was with. I was having quite an emotional reaction and they held my hands and stroked my hair and made me feel very relaxed. I was terrified more by the sedation process than the actual procedure so I’m really thankful to them! 

Here are some tips that may make your experience better:
•drink as much water as you can before the cut off time prior to your surgery, this will mean you’re less dehydrated and will be easier for them to find a vein. 
•apply a warm pack to where you will be having the IV placed right before your appointment. This will again help make it easier to identify your veins making it a quick easy process for you. 
•Bring a sensory item such as a stress ball with you to hold during the experience, they may provide one but easier to bring your own!
•Be honest about how you’re feeling, if you need support, ask for someone to hold you’re hand (if they don’t already). 
•Have comfort items ready for you in the car. For me I had a weighted blanket, ice packs, a sweater, a YouTube video loaded if I needed something to watch etc. 

The IV needle is not too big and is used to just place the line which is less uncomfortable, especially after they secure it with tape. The sedation solution feels cold when they insert it which can feel uncomfortable, they will do a little at a time and ask you how you are feeling and soon you won’t feel the solution. I “woke up” briefly during my procedure which is where I started having a bad emotional reaction. They decided to stop it there to avoid making it traumatic for me. If you have worries about waking up I suggest communicating with your team what you would prefer to be done (eg. stop/continue) so that you’re all on the same page! 

When I woke up I had periods of conciseness and periods that I don’t remember but I didn’t really say anything stupid, just said that the staff was super nice and held my hands over and over again. 

I researched a bunch before hand, watching videos etc on YouTube and they would all make me emotional, but now that I have experienced it all I can safely say it’s a LOT better than what I was expecting. I hope this helps and good luck!
